concept.name: Williams percent R
concept.definition: Larry Williams' momentum oscillator showing where the close sits relative to the highest high of the look-back period, plotted on an inverted 0 to -100 scale; mathematically the inverse of the fast stochastic %K line.
concept.intuition: It answers 'how close is the latest close to the top of the recent range?': readings near 0 mean closes at the range top, readings near -100 mean closes at the bottom.
concept.mechanics: Subtract the close from the highest high of the last n periods (default 14), divide by the high-low range, and multiply by -100. Readings from 0 to -20 are conventionally overbought, -80 to -100 oversold; the -50 centerline and momentum failures (failed retests of -20) give additional signals.
concept.failure_modes: Like all range-position oscillators it sticks at extremes during strong trends and whipsaws across the -50 centerline in choppy markets.
concept.misconceptions: Overbought (above -20) does not mean sell: sustained closes near the top of the range signal persistent buying pressure, and %R can stay overbought through an entire uptrend.
concept.example: Highest high 110, lowest low 100, close 103: %R = ((110-103)/10) x -100 = -70; a close at 108 gives -20.
